title: Negative COVID-19 Vaccine Information on Twitter: Content Analysis
screen_reason: Manual content analysis of 7306 COVID-19 vaccine-related tweets reporting the share coded anti-vaccine (1.8%, 131/7306) and the share coded negative vaccine information (21%, 1533/7306). The anti-vaccine share is a share of items in a sample carrying an anti-vaccine/implicitly misleading label, so the paper clears the CONTENT bar on a broad reading; the coding is stance-based rather than veracity-against-ground-truth, which is flagged (borderline) on both rows. The NVI category is coded QUALITY because the authors state explicitly that it can be factually true.

estimates.country: United States, United Kingdom, and Canada
estimates.date: Tweets collected December 23, 2020 to April 30, 2021; analysed tweets restricted to January 6 to April 30, 2021
estimates.measure_type: % of COVID-19 vaccine-related tweets manually coded as anti-vaccine
estimates.denominator: 7306 manually coded English-language tweets randomly sampled from a sampling frame of 217,954 COVID-19 vaccine-related tweets geolocated to the United States, United Kingdom or Canada
estimates.definition: A tweet was first coded 1 if its text contained negative information or sentiment about vaccines; those coded 1 were then split into tweets that were implicitly or explicitly anti-vaccine (this numerator) versus the remainder, classified as negative vaccine information
estimates.misinfo_def: "we use the concept of negative vaccine information (NVI) to describe content that characterizes vaccines or vaccination in a negative way without also expressing anti-vaccine sentiment"
estimates.source_quote: We found that 1.8% (131/7306) of tweets were anti-vaccine, but 21% (1533/7306) contained negative vaccine
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results (p. 1); the same counts appear in Results, first paragraph (p. 4): "Of the 7306 tweets, 131 (1.8%) were coded as anti-vaccine and 1533 (21%) were coded as NVI." (that sentence is split across the PDF's two columns, so the abstract sentence is quoted instead)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Four authors hand-coded mutually exclusive subsamples after training on a separate sample of 200 tweets; on 300 tweets coded by all four, 80% (n=240) had full agreement on anti-vaccine content, Krippendorff alpha=0.25; 79% (n=237) full agreement on NVI, Krippendorff alpha=0.63. The authors themselves call the anti-vaccine agreement 'at best, fair'.
estimates.moderator_quote: all 4 authors read through mutually exclusive subsamples of 8800 tweets and coded every tweet in which the text contained negative information or sentiment about vaccines as “1”; otherwise, the tweets are coded as “0.”
estimates.notes: Construct call for an adjudicator: the label is a stance/sentiment judgement ('implicitly or explicitly anti-vaccine'), not a truth/falsity judgement against an external ground truth, and the authors elsewhere treat anti-vaccine content and misinformation as separate categories ('Early negative impressions about vaccines that were neither anti-vaccine nor misinformation'). A wholly true tweet expressed with anti-vaccine sentiment would receive the label, which under the QUALITY-vs-CONTENT rule argues for QUALITY. I kept CONTENT because anti-vaccine health content falls inside the review's broad 'misleading (health) content' criterion, but flagged borderline=true. Interrater reliability for this specific code is very low (alpha=0.25), and the authors declined to analyse the anti-vaccine data further for that reason.

estimates.country: United States, United Kingdom, and Canada
estimates.date: Tweets collected December 23, 2020 to April 30, 2021; analysed tweets restricted to January 6 to April 30, 2021
estimates.measure_type: % of COVID-19 vaccine-related tweets coded as negative vaccine information (negative about vaccines but not anti-vaccine)
estimates.denominator: 7306 manually coded English-language tweets randomly sampled from a sampling frame of 217,954 COVID-19 vaccine-related tweets geolocated to the United States, United Kingdom or Canada
estimates.definition: Tweets whose text contained negative information or sentiment about vaccines (statistics or reports of adverse reactions, personal statements about adverse reactions, skepticism toward vaccine developers, policy decisions to stop or delay administration, expressions of concern) but which were judged NOT to express anti-vaccine sentiment
estimates.misinfo_def: "we use the concept of negative vaccine information (NVI) to describe content that characterizes vaccines or vaccination in a negative way without also expressing anti-vaccine sentiment"
estimates.source_quote: We found that 1.8% (131/7306) of tweets were anti-vaccine, but 21% (1533/7306) contained negative vaccine
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results (p. 1); the same counts appear in Results, first paragraph (p. 4): "Of the 7306 tweets, 131 (1.8%) were coded as anti-vaccine and 1533 (21%) were coded as NVI." (that sentence is split across the PDF's two columns, so the abstract sentence is quoted instead)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Four authors hand-coded mutually exclusive subsamples; on 300 shared tweets, 79% (n=237) full agreement on NVI, Krippendorff alpha=0.63.
estimates.moderator_quote: the media reporting of genuine adverse reactions to vaccines or infections among vaccinated individuals could increase concerns in the value of vaccination without being factually untrue or expressing an anti-vaccine opinion
estimates.notes: Coded QUALITY, not CONTENT: the authors state explicitly that NVI need not be false ('without being factually untrue'), give as NVI exemplars true EMA and Moderna news reports, and argue NVI 'could be promoted as evidence of an effective communication system'. A wholly true item receives the label, so this is a negativity/tone measure, not a prevalence-of-falsehood measure. Row kept for the record and flagged for exclusion from prevalence. definition_variant=true: it is the broader negative-content category in the same country x platform cell as the anti-vaccine row (the two categories are mutually exclusive by construction).

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, with reasons: (1) NVI by vaccine developer -- Oxford/AstraZeneca 35.69% (713/1998), Moderna 15.81% (204/1290), Pfizer-BioNTech 16.34% (477/2920), Other 14.37% (139/967) -- these are sub-corpora of the same measure, not the headline figure, and are QUALITY anyway. (2) Table 2 anti-vaccine and NVI shares by author type (government 0/140, media 3/1755 = 0.17%, medical 0/1078, other 108/4032 = 2.68%, closed/restricted 19/300 = 6.33%): author-type subgroups, not the paper's headline. (3) NVI prevalence BY COUNTRY: the country-specific percentages live in Figure 1, whose numbers are not in the text; the text gives only the distribution of NVI tweets across countries (UK 37.9%/581, US 49.7%/762, Canada 12.4%/190), which is a within-misinfo composition, not a prevalence, and the Discussion's 'More than 25% of Twitter content authored in the United Kingdom appeared to be NVI' is approximate and not R8-verbatim. So the pooled multi-country row is the only defensible geographic level. (4) '3 of the 4 coders yielding less than 2% of their tweets as anti-vaccine' -- a range statement about coders, not an estimate.

rob.design: Cross-sectional manual content analysis. Sampling frame: Twitter API (rtweet) keyword search on COVID-19 x vaccine terms, Dec 23 2020-Apr 30 2021, 7,827,949 tweets after removing retweets, narrowed by vaccine-brand terms to 785,107, then by author country/location/description fields to US/UK/Canada, English-only, >=1 follower, giving 217,954. 9000 tweets randomly sampled with replacement; 7306 analysed after dropping tweets outside Jan 6-Apr 30 2021 and the 300 reliability tweets. Four authors coded mutually exclusive subsamples after training on 200 tweets. Reliability on 300 commonly coded tweets: NVI 79% full agreement, Krippendorff alpha=0.63; anti-vaccine 80% full agreement, Krippendorff alpha=0.25. No response rate applies (observational platform data). Limitations acknowledged: search terms omitted anti-vaccine alternative spellings (likely underestimates anti-vaccine tweets); georeferencing dropped many tweets.
rob.item6_quote: In this study, we use the concept of negative vaccine information (NVI) to describe content that characterizes vaccines or vaccination in a negative way without also expressing anti-vaccine sentiment.
rob.item10_quote: Of the 7306 tweets, 131 (1.8%) were coded as anti-vaccine and 1533 (21%) were coded as NVI.
